areas.title: Perovskite Solar Cells
description: Co-authored studies on perovskite solar cells have focused extensively on small-molecule hole-transporting materials. Anthracene-, indolocarbazole-, dihydronaphthopentaphene-, spiro-, cyclopentadithiophene-, pentafulvalene-, dithienopyran-, and fused dithienoheterocycle-based structures were assessed through optical, electrochemical, thermal, mobility, morphology, and device measurements. Several studies compared fluorinated derivatives with non-fluorinated analogues, examining energy-level alignment, hole mobility, interfacial charge extraction, film formation, hydrophobicity, and device stability. Scalable implementations included a dopant-free hole-transporting material deposited by thermal-assisted blade coating and fluorinated materials applied to bar-coated perovskite films.

First-author experimental work investigated preheating followed by moderate-temperature liquid-medium annealing and FABr passivation, as well as chemical-bath-deposited SnO₂ on mesoporous TiO₂ electron-transport layers. Related co-authored experiments examined cesium iodide in two-step deposition, delayed annealing with KI/I₂, Tween 20 additives during thermal blade coating, and PVDF-HFP modification. The PVDF-HFP studies tested vacuum and gamma irradiation, and combined vacuum–light and vacuum–heat conditions; the combined-stress study used interface-specific recombination and lifetime analyses. Proton irradiation of single-junction devices and failure pathways of two-terminal tandem devices under space stressors were examined in separate reviews. An interlaboratory round-robin study compared current density–voltage and external quantum efficiency measurements for large-area devices and identified irradiance, spectral mismatch, temperature control, and measurement procedures as sources of variation.

areas.title: Redox Flow Batteries
description: A co-first-author experimental study of vanadium redox flow batteries modified graphite-felt electrodes with nanostructured graphitic carbon nitride by thermal polymerization. The work related graphitic-carbon-nitride distribution and electrode wettability to charge-transfer resistance, electrochemical activity, polarization, energy efficiency, and cycling performance. Under the reported conditions, optimized decoration improved electrolyte access, and the cell showed negligible degradation over 1000 cycles.

A separate co-authored review surveyed metal–organic-framework- and covalent-organic-framework-containing separators and membranes for redox flow batteries. It examined how pore size, functional modification, wettability, ion selectivity and permeability, processability, and scale-up affect separator design, while identifying this technology as being at an early stage. This contribution is a literature review rather than experimental membrane work.

areas.title: Dye-Sensitized Solar Cells
description: First-author work on dye-sensitized solar-cell photoanodes used tetrapod-like ZnO to establish electron-transport networks and multiple room-temperature electrophoretic depositions to form crack-reduced TiO₂ films on flexible ITO/PEN substrates. Electrochemical impedance spectroscopy and thickness-dependent current measurements were used to assess electron diffusion. Related co-authored studies examined solvothermally grown branched ZnO, tetrapod morphology and electrolyte additives, and ionic-liquid diffusion through porous ZnO electrodes. Separate studies evaluated microporous TiO₂ with in situ cross-linked gel-polymer electrolytes and chemically polymerized PEDOT, with or without carbon nanotubes, as counter electrodes.

Flexible titanium-substrate cells were studied with a sponge-like TiO₂ interfacial layer formed by peroxide oxidation and with mesoporous SiO₂ decoration in bifacial and back-illuminated configurations. Long-term tests on plastic dye-sensitized solar cells compared organic iodides, sealing conditions, and ITO/PEN sheet resistance during prolonged illumination and 60 °C thermal stress. A later first- and corresponding-author study of 5 × 5, 10 × 10, and 10 × 15 cm modules examined TiO₂ pretreatment and post-treatment, dye concentration and soaking temperature, electrolyte injection, module design, and polymer sealing.
